conviction_note: The evidence on what Winnebago will report leans slightly negative. Industry wholesale shipments for its Jun-Aug quarter fell about 14% in towables and 13% in motorhomes, Thor reported motorized margins down 600bp, the RVIA's Oct-16 forecast puts calendar 2026 at the bottom of WGO's own 290-310k assumption and 2027 flat at 285k, and a Chris-Craft trade-name impairment test is scheduled in the 10-Q. All of it is industry-public, and the stock sits at a 52-week low (-20% in 20 sessions, put skew +9.4), so the negatives agree with what the market already prices. Short interest is 10% of float, and this name rallied +13% on a miss-and-cut in June and +28.5% on last October's first full-year guide. That leaves p_up at 48 (a weak lean) on a large expected move of 12%. Findings sum to -0.8 and the scaled number is -0.48; both are small because what decides the reaction is the FY27 guide, which no document reveals.
bar: Q4 FY26 consensus adj EPS ~$0.46-0.50 on revenue ~$660-665M: Benzinga preview $0.47 / $660.25M (https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-stock-ratings/price-target/26/10/62464543/winnebago-earnings-are-imminent-these-most-accurate-analysts-revise-forecasts-ahead-of-earnings-call-2); EarningsWhispers $0.50 / $664.76M; TipRanks $0.46. Company guide (8-K 2026-06-25, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000107687/000162828026045356/exh9912026q3earningsrelease.htm): FY26 revenue $2.65-2.75B and adj EPS $1.65-2.00, against 9M actuals of $2,058.8M and $1.31. That implies Q4 revenue of $591-691M (midpoint $641M) and adj EPS of $0.34-0.69 (midpoint ~$0.52). On the Q3 call management said Q4 sales would be 'down double digits' from $777.3M and margins 'flattish to last year'. So consensus revenue sits in the upper half of the guide and EPS a little below the midpoint. FY27 consensus is not reliably sourced: one aggregator shows $2.99, which is probably stale from before the cuts. The FY27 bar is therefore unsourced and the guidance finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,686,960 shares = 9.99% of float, 4.2 days to cover, as of the 2026-09-30 settlement published 2026-10-09, up 5.5% from 2,546,427 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/WGO/short-interest). The sweep had 10.2% / 6.0 DTC (Equibles, Aug) and 12.4-12.8% (Benzinga, Aug). Skew 25d +9.35 vol points means downside is paid for; the put/call OI ratio is 0.88 on thin OI (807) with a wide ATM spread (29% of mid). Spot $22.49 is at its 52-week low, -54.9% from the high, -20.4% over 20 sessions and -2.9% over 5. Citi cut its target to $24 on 2026-10-13 and Weiss downgraded to sell on 2026-10-14. This is a moderately crowded short into a beaten-down name, and the options already price downside.

findings.finding: RVIA wholesale shipments for WGO's fiscal Q4 (Jun-Aug 2026) were down about 14% in towables and about 13% in motorhomes. Towables: Jun 22,728 (-14.3%), Jul 17,754 (-9.8%), Aug 20,790 (-16.9%). Motorhomes: Jun 2,756 (-1.6%), Jul 2,194 (-25.6%), Aug 2,809 (-11.7%). Motorhomes (46% of WGO's 9M revenue and its only growth segment, +17% YoY in 9M) turned sharply negative, against a hard comparison of Q4 FY25 motorhome revenue of $361.2M (+17.3%). Applying these rates to the Q4 FY25 segment base (towable $306M, motorhome $361M, marine $95M), plus WGO's towable share loss (Q3 units -26.5% against an industry of about -17%), gives about $645-655M. That is roughly 1-2% under the ~$660M consensus but inside the company's own 'down double digits' guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-06-25): revenue $698.7M against ~$777M consensus (-10%) plus a guide cut, and the stock rose +13.24%. Q4 FY25 (2025-10-22): revenue beat ($777M against $744M) plus the first FY26 guide, +28.53%. Revenue misses have not been punished on this name lately.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $660M sits above the guide midpoint ($641M) despite three months of industry data released after the June guide. If the market had marked revenue to the shipment series, the published revenue consensus would sit nearer $645M. Against that, the stock is -20% in 20 sessions with put skew, so the price may already embed it even if the published consensus does not.
findings.independence: July and June data come from separate RVIA releases (https://rv-pro.com/news/july-wholesale-shipments-near-20k-units-down-11-9-from-2025/, 2026-08-25; https://rv-pro.com/news/rvia-june-rv-shipments-down-13-1-yoy/). Camping World Q2 (2026-07-29) had same-store new units -16.3% and expected July to be 'more acute' (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729469894/en/). It is an industry proxy, not WGO's own number, and Class B vans (WGO's strength) were +19.5% in June, which partly offsets.

findings.finding: The RVIA fall RoadSigns forecast (published 2026-10-16) cut calendar-2026 wholesale shipments to ~290,000 (range 284,600-295,400, from a 314k median in the summer edition and 349k in spring). That is at the very bottom of WGO's own CY26 assumption of 290-310k. It projects CY2027 'relatively flat' at ~285,000 (274,700-295,300), with year-over-year growth only in H2 2027. WGO's first FY27 guide tomorrow will be built on that industry base, so it likely implies flat-to-down revenue from ~$2.65-2.70B, with any EPS growth coming from footprint and cost actions rather than volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First full-year guide in October 2025 (FY26 adj EPS $2.00-2.70 against $2.24 consensus): +28.53%. Guide cut in June 2026 (to $1.65-2.00 against ~$2.27 consensus): +13.24% (relief). Guidance changes move this stock a lot and not always in the direction of the number.
findings.why_not_priced: Published four sessions before the print and two days after Citi's cut. If FY27 estimates were already marked to a flat 285k industry, the published FY27 consensus would be near FY26's ~$1.75-1.80 rather than the $2.99 still visible on aggregators. But the street FY27 bar is unsourced, and the stock's 20-day drop plus put skew suggest much of this is in the price, so the finding is capped small.
findings.independence: Thor (2026-09-22) deferred FY27 guidance, expects 'relatively flat' retail and still says it can 'materially improve its earnings profile' through >$100M of cost actions (https://rv-pro.com/news/thors-q4-fiscal-2026-more-challenging-than-anticipated/). That cuts both ways: WGO also has footprint actions with 'benefits expected in fiscal 2027' (Q3 release).

findings.finding: Thor's quarter to 31 July 2026 (overlapping two of WGO's three Q4 months) had North American Motorized gross margin down 600bp on units -13.1%, 'higher promotional activity' in both towables and motorized, and fifth-wheel units -34.7%. Fifth wheels are Grand Design's core, and WGO management singled them out as under 'targeted pressure'. WGO guided Q4 gross and EBITDA margins 'slightly lower sequentially but flattish to last year' (Q4 FY25 adj EBITDA $38.2M, 4.9%). Thor's read-through puts that margin guide at risk, especially in towables. Net of the rest of the company, WGO's motorhome segment starts from a near-zero margin in Q4 FY25 (-0.1%), so its year-over-year comparison is easy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26: gross margin 13.6% against 13.7% (flat) with an EPS miss of $0.66 against $0.82, and the stock rose +13.2%. Margin disappointment has not been the line this stock sold on recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS at $0.47 already sits below the ~$0.52 guide midpoint, so part of this is in the bar. What would show it fully priced is consensus nearer the bottom of the guide ($0.34-0.40). The peer print is a month old and the stock has fallen since, so most of it is likely priced.
findings.independence: The Thor 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000730263/000073026326000028/thoq4fy26-earningsrelease.htm) is the same underlying document as the RV PRO write-up. Camping World cut its FY26 EBITDA guide on weaker new-unit gross profit (businesswire, 2026-07-29). Both are peer proxies, not WGO's own data.

findings.finding: Positioning: short interest is 9.99% of float (2.69M shares, 4.2 days to cover, 2026-09-30 settlement, up 5.5%) into a stock at its 52-week low ($22.49, -55% from the high, -20% in 20 sessions), with a 5.8-6.4% dividend yield. findings.finding: On 2026-08-20 WGO entered a Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement with JPMorgan as agent. It extends the up-to-$350M asset-based revolver to 2031-08-20 at SOFR +1.25-1.75%, and it is undrawn. Together with the $100M note redemption already done in FY26 (long-term debt $442.9M against $540.5M at FY25 year-end), the money buys liquidity and maturity runway, not a ramp or distress. Management also guided a further working-capital release in Q4, so Q4 cash flow could fund debt reduction or support the dividend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing. Net leverage of 3.0x (Q3) was flagged on the call as the balance-sheet priority.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two months. The only unpriced piece is the Q4 cash-flow and leverage print, which would show up as a lower net-leverage figure in the release. It is small.
findings.independence: 10-Q for Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000107687/000162828026045496/wgo-20260530.htm): ABL undrawn, debt $450M gross. Shares the 8-K's subject matter but is a separate document.

findings.finding: Marine read-through. MasterCraft's FQ4 call (2026-09-10) described pontoons as soft and promotional ('hasn't really got going yet'), took an impairment on Crest pontoon intangibles, and expects industry retail -5% to -10% over the next six months. Barletta (pontoons, gaining share at 9.3% TTM) is most of WGO's Marine segment: 13% of 9M revenue, Q3 revenue -8.3% and margin -350bp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marine has never been the line a WGO print turned on; it is 13% of revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: A small segment peer read that few RV-focused analysts carry. It would be priced if WGO marine estimates had been cut after September 10, and no such cut is visible.
findings.independence: WGO's own Q3 release: Marine revenue -8.3% and margin -350bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000107687/000162828026045356/exh9912026q3earningsrelease.htm). Shares a theme with the impairment finding below, but this one is about operating results.

findings.finding: The Q3 10-Q states WGO 'will perform a quantitative impairment assessment of the Chris-Craft trade name' in Q4 FY26 and warns of a possible charge (indefinite-lived trade names $352.3M in total, Marine goodwill $136.1M). Separately, market cap of ~$640M is about half of book equity ($1,234.4M), against $484.2M of goodwill: a classic impairment trigger for the annual Q4 test. A charge would hit reported EPS (excluded from adjusted) and is not quantified anywhere.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WGO took a $30.3M goodwill impairment in Q4 FY24 (shown in the Q4 FY25 release comparison). That October 2024 print is outside the baseline's 8-event window, so its reaction is not sourced here.
findings.why_not_priced: No preview mentions a charge, and reported-EPS estimates are not set to absorb one. If priced, reported-EPS consensus would sit well below adjusted. It is a non-cash item below operating income and is usually looked through, so it is filed at a fraction of its dollars.

baseline_tension: The fundamental negatives agree with the put skew and the -20% run-up, so they are probably priced. Positioning (10% short at a 52-week low) and the name's habit of rallying on clearing prints cut against them, so p_up sits only marginally below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5/6 (proxy, inside the guide): the RVIA wholesale finding lands inside management's 'down double digits' Q4 guide and is an industry proxy, so it went from -0.5 to -0.3.

Lesson 7 (sign agrees with a strong put skew, 10% short float): the FY27 industry-forecast negative went from -1.0 to -0.8 and the Thor margin read-through from -0.7 to -0.5. The positioning finding was left at +1.5.
Lesson 2 (an unquantified reported-quarter impairment is the exception that has paid): the Chris-Craft/goodwill impairment finding was refiled under reported_quarter and raised from -0.4 to -0.6.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the refinancing buys runway on an undrawn ABL with no distress signal, so it stays a small positive (+0.2).
Lesson 1 (the reaction function has a veto): p_up moved from 47 to 48, because a miss-and-cut was bought +13% last print.
